en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:0: It was midnight. Nandini's red saree was shining in the dim light of the lamp kept near the curtain. Kabir was standing behind him. Placing one hand on her arm, he leaned in to place a kiss on her shoulder. Nandini closed her eyes and turned her head back a little.
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:1: A smile was about to appear on his lips. When Kabir's beard touched her shoulder, she felt tickled. He pressed his lips to stop laughing.
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:2: “Why are you laughing?” Kabir asked softly. "How do you know? You are behind me."
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:3: “When you stop laughing, your shoulders shake.” This time Nandini did not even try to stop laughing.
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:4: She raised one hand and gathered her hair back. The bangles on her wrist tinkled and the earring touched her cheek.
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:5: Kabir put his arms around her waist. Nandini held his hand with her free hand.
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:6: She shrank a little more in his arms, and Kabir kissed her lightly on the cheek.
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:7: “Okay, now tell me,” she said with her eyes closed, “Still laughing?”
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:8: Kabir remained silent for a few moments. Then he said, “We will have to see this time.” He loosened his arms a bit.
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:9: Nandini removed her hand from her hair and slowly turned towards him. The red pallu slipped from her shoulder and rested on her arm.
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:10: Now both were face to face. Nandini's hand rested on his white shirt. "So?" he asked, raising his eyelids.
en:aadhi-raat-ki-muskaan:11: Kabir was about to answer when he too started laughing. Both of them stood there looking into each other's eyes and kept smiling.

en:aadhi-raat-ki-phusphusahat:4: So Meera also started laughing. “See? That's what she was saying.” Meera tilted her head back a little.

en:aadhi-raat-ki-phusphusahat:9: “If I had told you, you would have asked, for how long?” A smile appeared on Meera's lips.

en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-raaz:2: Nandini didn't say anything, just placed her hands on his. Kabir pulled her closer, but his grip was very soft. The utensils kept in the kitchen and the clock on the wall were silent in their places.

en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-raaz:4: He put his arms around Kabir's shoulders. Kabir looked into his eyes, as if asking for permission without saying anything.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-raaz:5: Nandini answered him by lowering her eyelids. He came closer and placed a light kiss on her cheek.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-raaz:6: Nandini's smile became deeper, as if time had stopped there. "Why are you so quiet?" Nandini asked in a whisper.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-raaz:7: “Because today your eyes are saying everything,” said Kabir. Nandini laughed and placed her hand behind his neck.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-raaz:8: Her wavy hair flowed down her back, the flowers on her saree glittered in the light. Kabir supported her waist and came a little closer.

en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-raaz:11: The same soft light of the kitchen was still spread around them. And their hidden secret became deeper in that one silent moment.

en:summary:ek-baar-phir-pyaar: He was sitting on a chair wearing white clothes in a room decorated with old photographs.
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:0: He was sitting on a chair wearing white clothes in a room decorated with old photographs. There was a slight smile and a little hesitation in his eyes behind the glasses. Then she came to him wearing a white saree and placed her arms on his shoulders.
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:1: His face was so close to hers that both of them kept smiling without speaking for a few moments. He said softly, “Even after all these years, you are the same.” Smiling, she asked, “And you? Have you really changed?”
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:2: “Some habits never change,” he replied. She laughed, then suddenly an old question returned in her eyes. Both of them got up from the chair and stood face to face.
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:3: He lovingly lifted her chin and looked into her eyes. “What happened? Do you want to say something?” he asked. She said softly, “When we parted, did you forget me?”
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:4: He remained silent for a few moments, as if searching for the right words. “If it had been easy to forget, I would not have been standing in front of you like this today.” The hesitation in her eyes now turned into a soft smile.
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:5: “I couldn't forget you either,” she admitted. “But I was afraid you wouldn't talk to me again.” He said, “When did you even try?”
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:6: She laughed and gently held the sleeve of his shirt. “So I'm trying today,” she said mischievously. “Just promise me one thing, this time you won’t go away quietly.”
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:7: He nodded, “And you won't leave things unfinished by getting angry.” She leaned a little more towards him and asked softly,
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:8: “Okay, so will you try our love once again?” The smile on her face was his first answer.
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:9: Then he took her hand in his and said, “Yes, but this time we will stay together.” She stood next to him, holding the pallu of the saree.
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:10: Now both of them were not avoiding anything like before. There was a peace on his face, which did not require words to express.
en:ek-baar-phir-pyaar:11: The pictures on the walls of the room were the same as they were some time ago. The story that remained incomplete between them got a new beginning.

en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:0: The evening's vegetables were slowly cooking in the small kitchen. Meera was standing in front of the stove in red saree. The Mogra Gajra of her hair was hanging from her shoulder.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:1: Raghav stopped behind the door and started looking at her silently. Meera heard his voice, but she did not look back. Raghav rested his hand on the wall and asked, “Why are you so quiet?”
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:2: While moving the ladle, Meera said, “Why did you have time to listen to me since morning?” Just then his mother came and stood at the door in green saree. Seeing his serious look, Raghav paused for a moment.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:3: Meera also saw them and silently reduced the flame of the gas. Only the sound of spices boiling remained in the kitchen. Raghav came a little closer, as if he wanted to appease her displeasure.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:4: He gently touched Meera's arm and said, “Listen, it was my fault.” Meera kept her eyes down, but a smile appeared on her lips. “Just saying sorry doesn't fix everything,” she said.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:5: Raghav asked in a low voice, “So what should I do?” Meera stirred the vegetables with a ladle and said, “Listen to me carefully sometime.”
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:6: The mother standing behind kept looking at both of them without saying anything. Raghav now came in front of her and held both her arms.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:7: Meera looked into his eyes for the first time, then lowered her eyes in shame. “From today onwards I will listen to everything you say,” said Raghav.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:8: “And when I get angry?” Meera asked softly. “Then I will come to convince you like this,” he replied smiling.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:9: The sternness on the mother's face standing at the door lessened a little. Perhaps they also understood that this was not a fight, but a small matter between two hearts.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:10: Meera said slowly, “First let me turn off the gas, otherwise the vegetables will burn.” Both of them laughed and mother also smiled slightly.
en:rasoi-mein-chhupa-pyaar:11: Raghav left her arm, but the love in his eyes did not diminish. That evening in that small kitchen, along with the vegetables, his anger also melted.

en:title:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz: The untold secret of the kitchen
en:summary:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz: There was soft evening light in the kitchen.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:0: There was soft evening light in the kitchen. Naina, dressed in green shiny kurti and olive dupatta, was making samosas. His hands were busy with the dough and filling kept in front of him.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:1: Then Dev came from behind and smiled and took her in his arms. Naina's hands stopped for a moment. He closed his eyes, but a smile appeared on his lips.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:2: Dev leaned close to her shoulder and asked softly, “Are you tired?” She laughed lightly, “Not because of work, but because of your mischiefs.” Dev softened his grip around her waist a little more.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:3: “So let me help you this evening,” he said. He looked at the half finished layer of samosa. “Help? You can't even roll the dough into a round,” Naina teased.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:4: Dev leaned closer to her and placed a light kiss on her cheek. Naina bowed her head as if she wanted to hide her laughter.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:5: Her closed eyelids and lovely smile gave the answer. For a few moments in the kitchen there was only slow laughter of both of them.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:6: “You know,” Dev said softly, “I come here every day for a reason.” Naina raised her eyebrows, “To eat samosas?”
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:7: “No, to see you smiling like this.” Naina extended her hand and held his hand.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:8: “So you kept this secret hidden for so long?” he asked. Dev smiled, “Yes, and got caught today.”
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:9: Naina slowly turned towards him and took her hand to his neck. Dev held her lovingly in his arms.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:10: He pressed against her cheek, and Naina closed her eyes again. The samosas in front were still incomplete.
en:rasoi-ka-ankaha-raaz:11: But that evening the most lovely thing was cooking in the kitchen – the silent, true love between the two.

en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:0: Sunlight was filtering through the window in the small room of the old house. Naina was standing in front of her father-in-law Raghuveer in pink saree. She was not surprised when Raghuveer held her face with both hands.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:1: He just raised his eyes and looked at them, as if an old question had come to the fore again. "Why were you looking away from me?" Naina asked softly. Raghuveer remained silent for some time.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:2: “Because there is talk about us at home,” he said. Naina's light smile disappeared in a moment. “We didn't even tell anyone,” she muttered.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:3: “Some things are visible even without being said,” Raghuveer replied. Both knew that it was no longer easy to hide the affection between them. Naina moved away from him and turned towards the window.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:4: She held back her tears as she looked through the bars. Raghuveer came and stood behind her and gently held her waist. She did not move away from them, but her eyes were still fixed on the window.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:5: "If everyone asked, what would you say?" he asked softly. Raghuveer said, “I will not hurt you further by lying.”
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:6: Naina folded both her hands in front of her, but did not say anything. After some time she turned towards him.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:7: This time there was a strange confidence along with fear in his eyes. He gently placed his hand on her shoulder.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:8: Raghuveer's hand was still on her waist. “I don't know what will happen tomorrow,” said Naina.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:9: "Me neither," he replied truthfully. Then both of them came so close that there was no need to take the matter further.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:10: Then loud voices of the family members started being heard from outside. Questions had been raised regarding their meeting.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-mulaqaat:11: Naina and Raghuveer still stood there, looking into each other's eyes. Their faces were almost touching, and unspoken emotions lingered in the silence of the room.

en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:1: As soon as she placed her lips on his cheek, Meera smiled and closed her eyes. Both of them loved each other many years ago. Then circumstances changed and their paths diverged.
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:2: Now Meera was married, but the memories had not gone anywhere. Today, after so long, they were face to face again.
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:3: Aarav asked softly, “Did you ever remember me?” Meera said, “Some people are not remembered, they always remain in the heart.”
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:4: Hearing this, Aarav remained silent for a few moments. He loosened his grip on Meera's waist a little.
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:5: “I don't want you to have any trouble because of me,” he said. Meera placed her hand on his hand.
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:6: “I know,” she said, “just let us live in this moment for a little while.” Aarav looked at her, and both of them smiled lightly.
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:7: After a while he sat on the edge of the bed. Meera placed one of her hands behind Aarav's shoulder.
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:8: Aarav took her into his arms again, holding her tight. Coming so close to her face, he stopped.
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:9: “When will we meet again?” he asked. Meera said softly, “Don't ask for the answer to that question right now.”
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:10: Aarav didn't say anything, just leaned closer to her cheek. Meera closed her eyes and a slight smile appeared on her face.
en:purane-pyaar-ki-mulaqaat:11: Both of them remained near each other like this for some time in the light of the room. That meeting reminded him that some relationships change with time, but not their memories.

en:title:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz: The secret of the heart hidden in the kitchen
en:summary:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz: Soft morning light was coming in through the kitchen window.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:0: Soft morning light was coming in through the kitchen window. Naina, dressed in a blue flowery suit, was placing hot pakodas on a plate. Then Kabir, wearing orange kurta, came behind and placed his hand on her shoulder.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:1: He kissed Naina's temple and she smiled shyly. Naina was the sister-in-law of this house and Kabir was her brother-in-law. They themselves could not understand when this closeness between the two became a heartbeat.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:2: Without looking at him, Naina asked softly, “What if someone sees?” Kabir loosened his hand and said, “If you say so, I will go away right away.” Naina turned and looked at him and gave a small smile.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:3: There was only silence for a few moments in the kitchen. With the aroma of pakodas, the hesitation of both of them gradually started reducing. Naina picked up the plate and offered a small pakoda towards Kabir.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:4: Kabir bent down and started taking bites from his hand. His eyes were on Naina's face, and Naina was not able to stop laughing. “How is it?” he asked lovingly.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:5: Kabir smiled, “It is from your hand, it will be good.” Naina averted her eyes, but happiness was clearly visible on her face.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:6: Both of them understood that it was not just about praising the pakodas. Naina became silent for some time as she put the plate back.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:7: She said softly, “What we feel is also fear.” Kabir said, “I don’t want to put you in any trouble.”
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:8: He extended his hand towards Naina, but this time he stopped. Naina herself came forward and held his hand.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:9: The answer was clear in his eyes, even if his lips could not say anything. Both of them realized that it would not be easy to hide this thing even from their hearts.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:10: Kabir came and stopped behind her, and Naina allowed him to come closer. Naina's eyelids drooped as he placed a gentle kiss on her cheek.
en:rasoi-mein-dil-ka-raaz:11: Both of them standing near the plate remained silent for some time. His untold secret had finally been revealed to him in that small kitchen.

en:title:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz: a secret hidden in the mirror
en:summary:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz: She was standing in a green saree in front of the old mirror kept in the room.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:0: She was standing in a green saree in front of the old mirror kept in the room. The bindi on her forehead, golden earrings and red-green bangles were shining. When her father-in-law held her by the waist, she slowly turned towards him.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:1: The faces of both were so close that words were lost for a few moments. She was sad inside for many days. Today the same sadness was clearly visible in his eyes.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:2: She put her arms behind his neck. He asked softly, “What is the matter, why do you remain so silent?” She kept looking at him for some time.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:3: Then she said, “Sometimes I feel like someone should understand without asking.” His gaze softened, and his grip tightened slightly. She slowly bowed her head and placed it on his chest.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:4: Now his eyes were closed and there was a slight smile on his lips. He handled her hair with one hand. Then placed a very light kiss on her forehead.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:5: The shadows of both were standing silently together in the mirror. In that moment he felt a strange peace.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:6: But at the same time a question also started arising in the heart. She was the daughter-in-law of his family, and this relationship brought with it many limitations.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:7: He moved away a little and brought down his hand which was on his shirt. He understood her hesitation, but did not say anything.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:8: She started adjusting her earrings, as if hiding her heartbeat. He looked into her eyes and slowly came closer.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:9: The next moment his lips touched her cheek. She paused, then looked at the mirror.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:10: There was surprise in his eyes, and an incomplete smile on his face. Father-in-law was still standing near him, but both were silent.
en:aaine-mein-chhupa-raaz:11: She knew that some closenesses were not easy. The mirror had seen that moment, but its meaning was still unspoken.

en:title:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz: The untold secret of the lonely daughter-in-law
en:summary:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz: The golden sunlight coming from the wooden windows was spreading into the room.
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:0: The golden sunlight coming from the wooden windows was spreading into the room. Nandini, dressed in yellow floral clothes, was sitting on the edge of the bed. Her father-in-law, Devendra ji, came near and gently took her in his arms.
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:1: When he kissed her cheek lovingly, a shy smile blossomed on Nandini's face. A lot had changed in this house after her husband passed away. The day would be spent in work, but in the evening Nandini would feel sad.
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:2: Devendra ji used to recognize his sadness even without asking. Today he asked softly, "Why are you so quiet?" Nandini looked at him and then lowered her eyes.
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:3: "When you're closer, it feels a little less lonely," she said. A slight smile appeared on his face also. Nandini shyly closed her eyes and tucked her hair behind her ears.
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:4: Devendra ji's arm was still around him. He asked in a soft voice, "Do you want to say something?" She remained silent for a few moments, then said, "There is one thing that I could not tell anyone."
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:5: "Not even me?" He asked. There was slight moisture on Nandini's eyelids. "I'm afraid people won't understand what I'm saying," she said.
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:6: Devendra ji looked at him and kept listening without interrupting. Nandini said softly, “Talking to you gives me great relief.” "Sometimes so much so that I cannot understand what my own heart is saying."
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:7: There was silence in the room for a few moments. He took her hand and said, "It is not necessary to name every feeling immediately."
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:8: "Your happiness and your honor come first." After listening to him the tension on Nandini's face started reducing.
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:9: She slowly placed her head on his shoulder and closed her eyes. Devendra ji caressed her hair and kissed her forehead lovingly.
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:10: Nandini's fingers stopped on his arm. There was the same sunlight outside the window, but the heaviness in his heart was now a little lighter.
en:akeli-bahu-ka-raaz:11: His big secret was not an incident hidden from anyone, but an unspoken feeling arising in his mind. And in that quiet moment, both of them understood each other's silence without saying anything.

en:title:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat: Unspoken love between landlady and tenant
en:summary:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat: Siya and Arjun were sitting together on an iron bench placed in front of the bamboo walls.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:0: Siya and Arjun were sitting together on an iron bench placed in front of the bamboo walls. Siya was the owner of that house, and Arjun was living there on rent for a few months. Siya was smiling in pink clothes, while Arjun placed his hand on her shoulder expressing his affection.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:1: Today even the silence between the two seemed like a sweet conversation. Siya asked with a light laugh, “Why do you become so silent every time I come?” Arjun smiled, “Because some things are not remembered after seeing you.”
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:2: “Okay sir, such big things!” Saying this Siya lowered her eyes. Arjun said softly, “To tell the truth, the best thing in this house is not this bench, it is your company.” Hearing his words, Siya's cheeks turned slightly red.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:3: She moved a little closer towards him and placed her hand near his hand. Arjun looked at him, but this time there was no need for either of them to say anything. After some time Arjun took out his phone.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:4: There was a picture of the same morning on the screen, in which both of them were seen laughing. Siya rested her head on his shoulder and looked at the picture carefully. “Why do I look so happy in this?” he asked softly.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:5: Arjun replied, “Maybe because your smile is not artificial.” Siya took his arm and said, “And maybe also because I had you.” Arjun smiled after listening to her and moved the phone a little closer.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:6: Then Siya took the phone in her hand and enlarged the picture and started looking at it. Arjun pointed towards the screen, “Look, here you are laughing and I am looking at you.” Siya giggled, “So whose picture was being taken, mine or yours?”
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:7: “For me, in every picture there is only you,” said Arjun. Siya smiled and held his hand. Seeing the shy happiness on her face, Arjun also remained silent for a few moments.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:8: There was a light breeze outside and the small corner between the bamboo walls was filled with peace. Siya said softly, “Arjun, people call us landlady and tenant.” “And what do you say?” Arjun asked.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:9: Siya took his hand in both her hands and said, “I say, you are mine now.” Arjun smiled and took her closer to him.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:10: Siya placed her head on his shoulder and closed her eyes. At that moment neither any promise nor big talk was necessary.
en:makan-malikin-ki-mohabbat:11: There were only two hearts, which had started understanding each other's heartbeat. That evening the simple iron bench became his most beautiful memory.

en:title:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur: The truth about the closeness of lonely daughter-in-law and father-in-law
en:summary:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur: That evening, Meera was standing silently near the bed in the small room of the house.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:0: That evening, Meera was standing silently near the bed in the small room of the house. There was a pink saree, a mogra gajra in her hair and hidden sadness in her eyes. Her father-in-law, Harinarayan ji, standing at the door, was observing her silence.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:1: Meera looked back, then lowered her eyes and said softly, “Babuji, everything is fine.” Harinarayan ji understood that she was not telling the truth. Meera was feeling lonely at home for many days.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:2: Her husband was in another city due to work, and there were less conversations on phone. Today something said by a relative had further hurt his heart. She stood with her hands resting on the bed, as if she was controlling herself.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:3: While handling her gajra, Harinarayan ji asked, “Daughter, why is the heart so heavy?” Meera's eyes filled with tears, but she still remained silent. He placed his hand lightly on her shoulder and simply said, “You are not alone in this house.”
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:4: There was no pretense in those words, there was true fatherly affection. Meera sat on the edge of the bed and folded her hands together. “Babuji, why do people misinterpret everything we say?” he asked softly.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:5: Harinarayan ji took a long breath; The whisperings raised in the neighborhood had now reached the relatives. Some people had termed his concern and trust in Meera as unnecessary suspicion. He said, “People's thinking cannot change the truth of our relationship.”
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:6: Meera said, “But my honor should not be lost in this noise.” “Honor does not come from remaining silent, but from standing up for the truth,” he replied. For the first time Meera raised her head and looked into his eyes.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:7: He saw neither any question nor any accusation there – there was only closeness. Harinarayan ji stepped back a little, so that he could sit comfortably.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:8: “Tomorrow I will speak in front of everyone myself,” he said in a calm voice. “And I will also speak, Babuji,” Meera said, gathering courage.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:9: There was silence in the room again, but now it was not as heavy as before. Meera wiped her tears and gave a small smile after a long time.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:10: Harinarayan ji placed his hand on his head for blessings. No matter how many stories the outside world created, there was a clear relationship in that room.
en:akeli-bahu-aur-sasur:11: It was a father's trust in his daughter-in-law, and a daughter's trust in her father-in-law. There was no chaos in the house that night, but the fear of loneliness definitely went away from Meera's heart.

en:college-ki-madam:2: He laughed, “And who will scold me so sweetly for every little mistake I make?” “The studies are over, but the mischiefs still remain,” Madam replied softly. He adjusted the bag from his shoulder and kept looking at them silently for a few moments.
en:college-ki-madam:3: Madam's smile remained, but her fingers held the edge of the books a little tightly. Both of them were thinking that they were going to remember this simple afternoon for a long time. As they walked, they stopped in a quiet corner of the corridor, where soft light was coming from a nearby window.
en:college-ki-madam:4: Madam stood against the locker and laughingly started straightening his crooked tie. “Having grown up so much, still can't tie a tie properly?” He teased. The student said in a low voice, “Maybe so that you get an excuse to fix it.”
en:college-ki-madam:5: Madam looked at him, then tried unsuccessfully to stop her laughter. For a few moments there was only eye contact between them and the silence of the afternoon spread around. There had been talk in college about their closeness, but there was no pretense in this moment.
en:college-ki-madam:6: Madam released his tie, but did not take her eyes off him and asked softly, “Aren't you afraid of those things?” He became serious, “People will keep talking, I am just afraid that you might get hurt.” Hearing this, a gentle smile appeared on madam's face.
en:college-ki-madam:7: He said, "That's why prudence is important. As long as you are my student, our boundaries should remain clear." He nodded, "I respect you. Don't want to ruin this relationship by doing anything rash."
en:college-ki-madam:8: Madam heaved a sigh of relief; He found his answer truer than any big promise. That day they realized that true love lies not only in coming close but also in understanding each other's dignity.
en:college-ki-madam:9: Then they came to the middle of the corridor and stood face to face, and madam gently placed her palm on his chest. He kept looking at them with one hand in his pocket, as if he wanted to preserve this moment in his memories forever.
en:college-ki-madam:10: “Take care of yourself,” madam said, and a sweet sadness entered her voice. “You too,” he replied smiling, “and when we meet again, please fix my tie again.”
en:college-ki-madam:11: Madam burst out laughing; The same old mischief returned in his eyes also. Their last smile remained in that quiet corridor of the college – an incomplete thing, which both of them kept in their hearts with respect, hope and a beautiful memory.

en:summary:makan-malik-ki-betii: The landlord's daughter was standing close to the wall in the light sunlight of the verandah.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:0: The landlord's daughter was standing close to the wall in the light sunlight of the verandah. The white flowers in her braids were slowly moving with the wind. The tenant came near him, so much so that there was only a breath's distance between them.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:1: He hesitantly kissed her cheek, and she remained silent for a moment. She looked up and asked, “Why did you come so close so suddenly?” The tenant stepped back a little. “If you don't like it, I walk away.”
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:2: She smiled lightly. “When did I tell you to go away?” Hearing his words, his eyes sparkled with long wait. The landlord's daughter looked at his face carefully, as if reading something unspoken.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:3: “Do you know how much chaos there would be if they found out about us?” He said softly. “I know,” he replied, “that's why your wish is most important to me.” He stepped forward and put his arms around the tenant's shoulders.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:4: He came closer to her and lovingly stopped near her cheek. He closed his eyes; There was now confidence on his face instead of hesitation. “Even in such silence, your heartbeat can be heard,” she said smiling.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:5: “And I remember everything you say,” she said softly. She laughed, then placed her hand on the back of his neck and held him close. For a few moments both remained lost in that feeling of belonging without saying anything.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:6: The tenant rested his head near his shoulder. The white flowers in her hair were touching her cheeks. The landlord's daughter held his shoulder and closed her eyes.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:7: They were realizing that coming close was easy, living together was difficult. “Will you hold my hand like this tomorrow also?” he asked very softly.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:8: He raised his head and said, “Yes, but not secretly, but with respect.” There was more truth in that answer than any big promise.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:9: She combed his messy hair and smiled. “So first keep your intentions so clear that no question can weaken us.”
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:10: The tenant nodded and looked into her eyes and said, “We will not be in a hurry.” She came closer to him again, this time without hesitation, and hugged him gently.
en:makan-malik-ki-betii:11: No matter how much chaos there was in the outside world over their closeness, in that quiet moment both of them chose that their relationship would move forward with trust, consent and respect.

en:title:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani: Unique story of daughter-in-law and father-in-law
en:summary:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kaha: The golden evening sunlight was shining in the small courtyard of the old house.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:0: The golden evening sunlight was shining in the small courtyard of the old house. The daughter-in-law standing in pink clothes was lost somewhere; There was an indescribable sadness on his face. The father-in-law standing behind gently held her shoulder and took her hand in his.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:1: She kept looking ahead, but her silence softened a little due to that affectionate touch. “What's the matter daughter-in-law, why are you so quiet today?” Father-in-law asked very lovingly. “Nothing,” she said, but it was clear from her voice that a lot was going on in her mind.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:2: The father-in-law did not ask any other questions; Just stand near him. After some time, the daughter-in-law herself said, “Sometimes I feel like no one understands what I say.” “It is not necessary to get answers to everything immediately,” he said softly.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:3: “Sometimes listening to someone without interrupting is a great help.” The daughter-in-law turned and looked at him, as if for the first time she had found the courage to speak her mind. A light breeze blew in the courtyard and the cloth hanging nearby started moving slowly.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:4: The father-in-law asked, “Do you want me to sit here and listen to you all?” The sternness on the daughter-in-law's face diminished; He nodded slowly. “I just want my voice to be respected in this house,” she said.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:5: “You are the daughter-in-law of this house, but first of all you are a person with your own thoughts and dreams.” Hearing this, her eyes became moist and she touched his shoulder affectionately. Her father-in-law gave her a light, affectionate kiss on her cheek, as if giving more assurance than words.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:6: The daughter-in-law remained silent for a few moments, then said, “You listened to me today, that is enough for me.” “And whenever you feel heavy, tell me,” replied the father-in-law in a calm voice. When she stood in front of him, he held her hands again.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:7: She placed her fingers on his palms and exhaled slowly. The father-in-law stood behind him, but this time there was no loneliness in his eyes as before. The daughter-in-law moved a strand of hair behind her ear and looked towards the courtyard.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:8: There was not a big smile on his face, just a small relief which was reaching his heart. “Can I say something?” He asked in a low voice. “Yes daughter-in-law, tell me,” he said.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:9: “I was afraid that you would also take a decision without understanding what I said.” The father-in-law replied, “Relations are not governed by age or authority, but by trust and respect.” Hearing this, the daughter-in-law pressed his hands lightly.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:10: That evening neither any big promise nor any miracle took place in the courtyard. Only a daughter-in-law got a place to express her views and a father-in-law listened to her patiently.
en:bahu-aur-sasur-ki-anokhi-kahani:11: The closeness between them was not of any show, but of respect and family affection. And perhaps this was the most beautiful ending of that unique story—where silence was replaced by trust.

He pointed towards the pan, “Turn now, it's the right time.” The next moment one of his hands came to rest on her waist; She was definitely surprised, but did not step back.
en:rasoi-mein-bahu-aur-sasur:5: “There is something going on in your mind,” he said softly. The father-in-law bowed his head and whispered near her ear, “There is one thing which I have kept hidden for months.” Now the daughter-in-law's smile was filled with curiosity along with mischief.
en:rasoi-mein-bahu-aur-sasur:6: He took out the bread from the pan and asked, “What kind of secret?” The father-in-law took out a small envelope from the kitchen cupboard and placed it in front of him. It contained copies of her favorite recipes and papers on how to start a small home-cooking business.
en:rasoi-mein-bahu-aur-sasur:7: The daughter-in-law looked at him surprised, “You did all this… for me?” “You always said that the food in your hands should have its own identity,” he said. “I wanted that when I tell you, your dream will no longer remain just a dream.”
en:rasoi-mein-bahu-aur-sasur:8: His eyes were filled with tears; His hidden secret for so long was actually a preparation for her happiness. She turned and came closer to him and remained silent for a few moments taking the support of his arms.
en:rasoi-mein-bahu-aur-sasur:9: The father-in-law then placed a gentle kiss on her cheek; This time there was more gratitude on his face than shame. “You did all this, and you didn't even let me know,” she said.
en:rasoi-mein-bahu-aur-sasur:10: He smiled and replied, “Some surprises go best with bread.” Then the daughter-in-law laughed and took out the next roti from the pan and both of them arranged it on the plate.
en:rasoi-mein-bahu-aur-sasur:11: Later, when the family came to know about that envelope, everyone was really surprised. But for the daughter-in-law, the most beautiful moment was the warmth of the kitchen, her silent courage and a dream which was now about to come true.

en:title:purane-dost-ka-raaz: Hidden secret of a beautiful girl and her old friend
en:summary:purane-dost-ka-raaz: Light sunlight coming from the window was spreading in the room.
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:0: Light sunlight coming from the window was spreading in the room. She was standing silently in a cream colored scarf and golden embroidered suit. His old friend was sitting in front, and his arms were gently placed around her waist.
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:1: Both of them were so close that as soon as their eyes met, something hidden for years appeared in their eyes. She smiled and said, “Why are you so quiet today?” The friend looked at him and said, “Because I am afraid to say something today.”
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:2: "To me as well?" he asked with surprise. “Most of all you,” he laughed lightly. He combed her scattered locks with his fingers, then placed his hand on her shoulder.
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:3: In this small touch of his, there was a closeness which was never lost in the long journey of friendship. For several moments both of them just kept looking at each other, as if words were no longer necessary. When she turned towards the window, her old friend also slowly came near her.
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:4: He took her in his arms from behind, but so lightly that she could easily move away if she wanted. She did not move; She placed her hand on his arm. The friend bent down and gave him a soft kiss on the shoulder.
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:5: A shy smile appeared on her face, and she asked softly, “Since when?” He remained silent for a few moments, then said, “Probably since the day we first became good friends.” He turned and looked at her; Now there was more relief than surprise on his face.
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:6: “Why didn’t you tell me all these years?” There was a slight complaint in his voice. “I thought if I told the truth, our friendship would change,” she replied. She laughed, then rolled her eyes and said, “And I thought you would never understand.”
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:7: He stopped short after hearing this. “Meaning…in your heart too?” “Yes,” she said softly, “but I also didn't want to lose our friendship.” This was the secret that both of them had kept hidden in their hearts for years.
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:8: The same truth that had kept them apart now brought them closer. She rested her fingers on the wooden table kept nearby and started looking outside the window. The old friend stood behind her and put his arms around her waist again.
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:9: He turned his head slightly; Near his face was his friend's face, eyes closed and breathing calm. “Now, isn't there anything to hide?” he asked mischievously.
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:10: “Just one thing,” he smiled, “I want to spend every morning with you like this.” She held his arms lightly and said, “Then never stop telling the truth from now on.”
en:purane-dost-ka-raaz:11: There was the same soft light in the room, but the world had changed for both of them. The old friendship had now become the beginning of a new, true love.

en:title:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi: A meeting between brother-in-law and sister-in-law on the roof of their house changed their lives!
en:summary:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi: The yellow clothes on the terrace were moving slowly in the wind on a sunny afternoon.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:0: The yellow clothes on the terrace were moving slowly in the wind on a sunny afternoon. Sister-in-law was sitting on the cot and brother-in-law had come and sat near her. He very gently tucked a lock of hair that had fallen on her face behind her ear.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:1: Sister-in-law closed her eyes, as if she had found solace in that small care. “Why are you so quiet today?” Brother-in-law asked in a low voice. Sister-in-law smiled, “Sometimes a lot is said even without speaking.”
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:2: He laughed, then seeing her smile he himself became silent. There was a blue sky above and the yellow saree on the rope nearby was rustling in the wind. When sister-in-law inclined her head towards his shoulder, he looked at her affectionately.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:3: A few moments passed between them in which no answer was needed. There was just wind, sunshine and an unspoken thing, which was slowly becoming clear. After some time, sister-in-law got up and started collecting her clothes.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:4: He extended his hand and tried to remove a yellow cloth, but the clip got stuck. The brother-in-law came back and said, “Wait, I will help.” Sister-in-law looked back, “Will you help or tease me?”
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:5: He smiled and said, “I will only help if you ask.” Their laughter echoed on the rooftop, and became brighter like sunshine. While handling the clothes, both of them came very close to each other.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:6: Brother-in-law gently took her in his arms, then stopped after looking into her eyes. Sister-in-law placed her hand on his arm and smiled lightly. “You know why this moment feels so good?” He asked.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:7: “Because you are happy?” He replied slowly. “Because there is no hurry here,” said sister-in-law, “there is only peace.” He placed his forehead against hers and understood it without words.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:8: Both of them looked into each other's eyes and then laughed secretly. When a gust of wind came, the yellow cloth hanging above started blowing again. Sister-in-law raised her hand and caught hold of its clip and brother-in-law held the other end.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:9: Their noses were almost touching, but both just kept smiling. “Should I leave now?” The brother-in-law asked pointing towards the clothes.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:10: Sister-in-law laughed, “Hold the cloth, let’s talk later.” He fixed the clip, but the smile on his face did not last long.
en:chhat-par-dewar-aur-bhabhi:11: No big promises were made that afternoon, and nothing heavy was said. Still, that one meeting became such a memory in their lives, which filled a new tenderness in both of their hearts.

en:title:akeli-makan-malikin: Unique story of a single landlady and her tenant
en:summary:akeli-makan-malikin: The light of the candles burning in the room was slowly trembling on the walls.
en:akeli-makan-malikin:0: The light of the candles burning in the room was slowly trembling on the walls. The landlady, wearing a red and golden saree, was sitting silently, as if she wanted to say a lot. The tenant standing behind him kept looking at him for a few moments, then slowly came closer to him.
en:akeli-makan-malikin:1: When he placed his hands on her waist, she smiled softly and closed her eyes. For many days a closeness had been growing between them, but both of them had never said anything openly. The landlady asked in a low voice, “Why are you so quiet?”
en:akeli-makan-malikin:2: The tenant leaned closer to him and said, “I am afraid that what I say might hurt you.” She smiled, “How will you know before you say it?” He gently placed his face near her neck, but stopped the next moment.
en:akeli-makan-malikin:3: “Can I be this close to you?” he asked. He placed his hand on hers, “As long as you have respect for me.” That answer added a new warmth to the silence between them.
en:akeli-makan-malikin:4: The tenant kissed her shoulder gently, and the landlady closed her eyes. The golden border of her saree was shining with the flame of candles. She placed one hand behind her head and remained lost in that peace for a while.
en:akeli-makan-malikin:5: “It's strange,” she said, “I often felt alone in such a big house.” The tenant asked, “And now?” Without looking at him she said, “Now it seems someone really listens to my silence.”
en:akeli-makan-malikin:6: The tenant handled the pallu of her saree and said, “I want to be the reason for your happiness, not trouble.” The landlady looked at him, “Then promise me, whatever happens, it will happen by telling the truth.” “Promise,” she replied without hesitation.
en:akeli-makan-malikin:7: When she got up, he took her hand respectfully, and both of them stood among the candles. She was in front of him and the tenant was behind him, but this time there was no unspoken hesitation between them. She placed her palms on his hands and tilted her head back slightly.
en:akeli-makan-malikin:8: The tenant stopped by her side and said, “I will never let you feel alone.” The landlady opened her eyes and turned towards him.
en:akeli-makan-malikin:9: “Loneliness doesn't end by being with someone, but by being understood,” she said softly. The tenant said, “So give me a chance to understand you every day.”
en:akeli-makan-malikin:10: He held her hands tightly, as if that one answer had given him a long-lasting confidence. The light in the room was still the same, but the meaning of that evening had changed for both of them.
en:akeli-makan-malikin:11: There was no grand gesture, no haste – just two hearts expressing their feelings honestly. That night there was a new beginning of respect, belonging and love in the house where till now there was only a rented relationship.

en:title:purane-premi-ka-raaz: The secret of a beautiful girl and her old lover
en:summary:purane-premi-ka-raaz: The girl was standing in the pale golden light, wearing a cream colored saree and red blouse, with white flowers decorated in her hair.
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:0: The girl was standing in the pale golden light, wearing a cream colored saree and red blouse, with white flowers decorated in her hair. Behind her, her old lover stopped silently, as if something that had been withheld for many years had finally returned to her. He very gently placed his hand on her arm and leaned close to her face and asked, “Are you still angry with me?”
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:1: The girl lowered her eyes; There was no answer on his lips, but an entire past season was hidden in his silence. A long time ago, both of them loved each other, but an incomplete conversation created such a distance between them that no one could cross it. She understood that he did not feel the need to look back, and he continued to believe that the girl had forgotten him forever.
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:2: Today when we suddenly came face to face, old questions resurfaced, but no one had the courage to ask them. “You know,” he said in a low voice, “I have tried to talk to you many times, but I have been scared every time.” The girl turned her head a little and asked, "What are you afraid of? I just wanted to hear the truth once."
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:3: Looking into her eyes he said, “I thought you had moved ahead in your life, so I did not interfere in your happiness.” Hearing this, the hardness on the girl's face slowly started melting, as if an old knot was waiting to be untied. She handled the pallu of her saree and said very softly, “Why did I move ahead? I was waiting for your return even on the last day.”
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:4: He was surprised. “But you said I shouldn't come to you again,” she reminded. The girl nodded. “I told you not to come to me until you speak the truth from your heart. You only listened to half of what I said.” This was the shocking secret: their separation did not start from any infidelity, but from an incomplete sentence.
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:5: They kept looking at each other for a few moments, then he came a little closer from his place. His hands slowly came to rest near the girl's waist, as if he was asking if he was allowed to be near her now. The girl took his hand; There was more confidence in this short answer than years of complaining.
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:6: She rested her forehead against his shoulder and whispered, “I didn't leave you, I just misunderstood your words.” The girl's eyes became moist, but this time she did not try to hide the tears. “And I took your absence as your answer,” she said, “while we both continued to live with the question.”
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:7: He said with a slight smile, “So today I say clearly, I loved you then and love you even today.” The girl shyly turned her face away; The flowers in her hair trembled with her slightest movement. He lovingly took her in his arms, but so gently that the girl could take a step back if she wanted.
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:8: She did not step back; Instead she placed her hand on his and turned towards him smiling. The golden light had become softer now, and the silence around them seemed like a sweet song. The girl raised one hand near her hair, then asked softly, “What if you had listened to me in full that day?”
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:9: He smiled. “So perhaps we did not live all these years considering our dearest memory as pain.” “Then from today onwards you will not leave anything incomplete?” he asked.
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:10: “Never,” he said, “and if I don't understand anything, I will ask you again, I will not go away.” The girl laughed and held his hand tightly in her fingers.
en:purane-premi-ka-raaz:11: She inclined her head slightly towards his shoulder, and he stayed close to her as if he had returned home. That evening their old love blossomed again not in the noise of any new promise, but in a fully heard truth and two quiet smiles.

en:title:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat: Unique love between landlady and tenant
en:summary:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabba: The landlady wearing a green saree was standing near the open door of the house.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:0: The landlady wearing a green saree was standing near the open door of the house. His tenant in white T-shirt was looking at him smiling. The soft afternoon light was falling on the wall, and both of their eyes were fixed on each other.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:1: She asked softly, “Why are you looking at me like that?” And he smiled slightly. “Because your smile looks different today,” said the tenant. Hiding her laughter she said, “You find praise in everything.”
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:2: “Not a compliment, I just say what I feel,” he replied. The landlady's green bangles tinkled softly when she handled the pallu of the saree. She was about to say something, but seeing the truth reflected in his eyes, she remained silent.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:3: Despite standing so close, both of them did not hurry; Keep living that moment slowly. Their small conversation between the silent walls in front started seeming like a sweet secret. Suddenly a strand of hair fell on his face.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:4: The tenant extended his hand and asked, “Should I remove it?” She nodded shyly, and he gently tucked the strand behind her ear. The landlady's smile deepened after receiving the light touch of his fingers.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:5: “Since when did you become so caring?” He asked in a low voice. “Probably the moment your happiness began to seem like my own,” he said. She kept looking at him, as if there was something very special hidden in this simple answer.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:6: After some time, when she turned, the tenant came near her and placed his arms lightly around her. Instead of retreating, he smiled and held her hand. “Should I stay like this?” he asked in a whisper.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:7: “Just a moment more,” said the landlady shyly. He lovingly placed a small kiss on her cheek, and she looked up, smiling. For both of them, it was not a big promise, just a true moment full of intimacy.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:8: The tinkling of her green bangles and the slow laughter of both of them made even the silence of the house lovely. After a few moments she stood in front of him and started looking into his eyes.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:9: “Will you smile like this tomorrow also?” he asked. The tenant said, “If you want, I will bring a smile every morning.”
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:10: The landlady laughed, “Then I will also give you a reason to smile every day.” He again handled the lock of hair near her cheek, and their eyes met once again.
en:makan-malikin-ki-nayi-mohabbat:11: Now this house was not just walls and rooms for him, but also some new, untold feelings. The unique love that started that afternoon taught both of them that sometimes life can change with a small smile.

en:title:shaadi-se-pehle-wada: A promise between the fiance and the bride-to-be before marriage
en:summary:shaadi-se-pehle-wada: The light of burning lamps and yellow lanterns in the room was making the sweet evening more beautiful.
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:0: The light of burning lamps and yellow lanterns in the room was making the sweet evening more beautiful. The bride sitting in a red embroidered saree had downcast eyes, but there was a slight smile on her lips. Her fiancé came close to her from behind and lovingly brought his face close to her cheek.
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:1: She closed her eyes for a few moments and got lost in that feeling of belonging. “Why are you so quiet today?” The fiancee asked softly. She smiled, “I am not silent… I am just thinking how much everything will change after marriage.”
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:2: “Afraid of change?” He said looking into her face. “A little,” he told the truth, “my home, my habits… and lest I forget myself.” Hearing this, the fiancee's smile softened.
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:3: He said, “I want you to come into my life, but not leave your life.” On hearing this, he slowly turned and looked at her, as if some unspoken fear had eased. When she got up, her fiancé put his arms around her waist and held her close to him.
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:4: He also took one hand above her shoulder and lovingly placed it near her neck. “Really? My dreams, my choices… everything will remain the same?” he asked smilingly. “Now both of our dreams will go together,” he replied, “but the dreams of one will not be buried under the dreams of the other.”
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:5: She laughed, “Are you talking big?” “No,” he also laughed, “It's a promise. And if I ever forget, just remind me.” She said mischievously, “Then I will remind you every day!”
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:6: The laughter of both of them mingled with the light of burning candles in the room. After some time, the bride-to-be said in a low voice, “I want not only love, but also a good friend.” The fiancé looked into her eyes and said, “So we will start each morning with friendship.”
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:7: “And when we fight over something?” he asked. “Then instead of silencing each other, we will listen to the whole thing first.” She held his hand and said, “And we will not leave each other's hand even if we are angry.”
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:8: “Sure,” she said, lacing her fingers with his. Now both were standing together; Golden light was falling on her red saree and her fiance's arms were around her. When the bride-to-be looked in front, there was no hesitation on her face like before, but a calm confidence.
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:9: She realized that marriage does not mean losing one's identity, it can also mean enhancing it with someone. The fiancee asked softly, “Still feeling scared?” She pressed his palm, “Yes, a little… but now I know I am not alone.”
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:10: “And neither do I,” he smiled. They stood near each other for some time without saying anything, as if all the further conversation had been absorbed in that silence.
en:shaadi-se-pehle-wada:11: No miracle happened that evening, they just learned to really listen to each other. That small promise made before marriage became the most beautiful beginning of their future life.

en:title:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz: Untold secret of fiance and his girlfriend before marriage
en:summary:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz: There was soft yellow light in the room and rose petals were scattered on the bed.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:0: There was soft yellow light in the room and rose petals were scattered on the bed. Mogra flowers were hanging from the braid of her girlfriend dressed in red and golden saree. Her fiancé came closer wearing a black shirt and lovingly put his arm around her shoulders.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:1: He closed his eyes, as if all the restlessness was slowly melting away in that one moment. “Why are you so quiet?” the fiancee asked softly near her ear. She smiled, but her fingers were still playing with her bangles.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:2: “Sometimes even great happiness can be scary,” she said in a low voice. The fiance came a little closer to her, then stopped so that he could comfortably look at her face. Their eyes met and all the sounds in the room seemed to get lost somewhere.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:3: He took her hand in his, and her girlfriend held his palm without saying anything. There was now that natural affinity between the two, which does not require words. “There is one thing which I have hidden from you till today,” the girlfriend suddenly said.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:4: Surprise appeared on the fiance's face, but he did not leave her hand. “On the engagement day, when you asked if I was happy or not, I just shook my head.” “You might have thought I was trying to understand this relationship.”
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:5: She took a deep breath and looked him straight in the eyes and said, “The truth is that I had given you a place in my heart long before that.” “I was just afraid that this relationship might be just a responsibility for you.”
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:6: He remained silent for a few moments, then a lovely sparkle appeared in his eyes. “And will you listen to my secret?” he asked smilingly. The girlfriend agreed shyly and held his hand a little tightly.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:7: “I also liked you for a long time, but never had the courage to say it.” “When I saw your silence on the day of engagement, I thought that maybe you don't consider me yours yet.” Both laughed at their misunderstanding; The hesitation of so many days went away in a moment.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:8: The girlfriend bowed her head, and the fiancé looked at her face lovingly. Slowly she leaned back on the pillow, and her fiancé came to rest beside her. He handled her hair with one hand and adjusted the pillow under her head with the other.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:9: Her laughter spread like a soft breeze amidst the fragrance of grass and rose petals. “So our biggest secret was that we both loved each other silently,” she whispered.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:10: “And now we will not remain silent on anything,” replied the fiance. She kept looking at him, the same confidence on her face that she had been looking for for years.
en:mangetar-ka-ankaha-raaz:11: That evening there were no big promises, no pretense, just two hearts recognized their truth. That meeting before marriage became for them the beginning of a story in which trust came before love.

en:title:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz: The untold secret of old love
en:summary:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz: A soft night breeze was blowing on the rooftop, and the shadows of the trees were standing silently in the distance.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:0: A soft night breeze was blowing on the rooftop, and the shadows of the trees were standing silently in the distance. Anaya was sitting near him, wearing a black printed saree, with a slight hesitation in her eyes. Aarav gently took her face in his palm and looked at her.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:1: Anaya lowered her eyelids, but could not hide the smile on her lips. “You still smile like that,” Aarav said softly. Anaya opened her eyes, “And you still take so long to say everything.”
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:2: Both of them laughed, but behind that laughter was a distance of many months. Sometimes they were very close to each other, then some unspoken things came in between. Today, meeting on the same roof after such a long time was like resuming an unfinished matter.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:3: Aarav's hand was still near her cheek, but she did not ask any questions. Perhaps he had realized that Anaya wanted to express her feelings herself. “You thought I forgot you?” Anaya asked in a calm voice.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:4: Aarav nodded, “That is what I had convinced myself.” Anaya held his wrist lightly and came closer. “The truth is that I never deleted your last message,” he said.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:5: “Whenever it felt like everything was over, I would read it and smile.” Aarav kept looking at her for a few moments, as if the old misunderstanding had suddenly lightened. “Then should we leave that silence here today?” he asked.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:6: Anaya smiled and said, “Yes, but a promise has to be made.” “Now you will not go away keeping anything in your heart.” Aarav took her fingers in his, “Never.”
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:7: She stood up slowly, and Aarav also stopped behind her. He placed his arms around her waist, as if asking if he could hold her. Anaya placed her hands on his arms and closed her eyes.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:8: That small gesture contained the confidence that both of them had been waiting for for so long. The night had become more quiet; The wind coming from the distance was shaking her earrings slightly. Aarav bowed his head near her shoulder and expressed his love very gently.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:9: Anaya tilted her head to one side, a carefree smile spread on her face. “Now tell me, did you remember me for so many days?” he asked softly.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:10: “Every day,” Aarav said, “just got the courage to say it today.” Anaya held his palms more tightly.
en:purane-pyaar-ka-ankaha-raaz:11: Now there was no big secret left – just the small fact that both of them had never forgotten each other. That night their old love on the rooftop resumed not with any noise but with a silent embrace.

en:title:office-ka-raaz: The most beautiful secret of the office
en:summary:office-ka-raaz: When Aarav lifted Siya's chin gently with his fingers, a shy smile appeared on her face.
en:office-ka-raaz:0: When Aarav lifted Siya's chin gently with his fingers, a shy smile appeared on her face. There was an open laptop in front, a mug of coffee and a small green plant were kept on the table. The office with large glass windows seemed completely quiet at that moment.
en:office-ka-raaz:1: Siya raised her eyes and looked at him and asked softly, “Why are you looking at me like that?” Aarav laughed. “Because my sweetest smile was hidden at work all day today.” Siya touched her wrist lightly. “You are my boss at the office, remember?”
en:office-ka-raaz:2: “And outside the office?” he asked mischievously. Instead of answering, Siya lowered her eyes. The pallu of her pink saree shifted a little, so Aarav lovingly corrected it.
en:office-ka-raaz:3: Even in such a small thing, Siya felt the same old thought of him. She smiled, but this time there was a little uneasiness in that smile. Aarav asked, "What happened? Why are you so silent today?"
en:office-ka-raaz:4: Sia said, “Sometimes it feels difficult to stay away from you in front of everyone.” “Me too,” Aarav admitted, “but I don’t want anyone to connect your hard work with our relationship.” Siya glanced at the laptop in front of him, where the files completed for the day were open.
en:office-ka-raaz:5: “I want people to recognize me for my work,” she said. “And that's what I love about you the most,” Aarav replied. Hearing his words, the hesitation in Siya's eyes slowly started melting.
en:office-ka-raaz:6: Aarav came closer to her, then kissed her forehead softly. Siya closed her eyes and held his arm for a few moments. “No one knows yet that we are husband and wife,” she said with a light laugh.
en:office-ka-raaz:7: “All they know is that you are my secretary and I am your boss,” Aarav smiled. “So when will you tell us this little secret of ours?” Siya asked. “The day you wish yourself. I will not say anything before your decision.”
en:office-ka-raaz:8: Siya held his hand a little more tightly. Aarav then bent towards her, placing both his hands on the table, so that their eyes were at the same height. Siya looked at him for a long time, as if reading the trust in his eyes that did not need words.
en:office-ka-raaz:9: “Tomorrow,” he said softly, “tomorrow we will tell everyone.” "Sure?"
en:office-ka-raaz:10: “Yes, but there is a condition. Praise me in the office only for my work.” Aarav laughed. “Okay, madam. And at home?”
en:office-ka-raaz:11: “At home…” Siya smiled and extended her hand towards him, “A little more love will do.” The laughter of both of them mingled in that quiet office, and the most beautiful secret between them no longer became a fear, but a sweet promise.

en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:0: Meera was sitting quietly and smiling in the pale yellow light of the room. The golden embroidery on her green clothes was shining and the vermilion on her forehead was enhancing the beauty of her face. Then Aarav, sitting behind, gently held her shoulder and lovingly placed his lips near her cheek.
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:1: Meera closed her eyes, as if she wanted to keep this small moment in her heart forever. Aarav smiled and asked, “What are you thinking?” Without opening her eyes, Meera said, “Are you this mischievous before or did you become so after marriage?”
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:2: Aarav laughed. “It was before too, I just didn't have the courage to tell you then.” Meera turned and looked at him. “So you kept hanging out as friends for so many years and didn't even say anything?” “I was afraid,” Aarav said softly, “that I might lose my best friend by speaking out of my heart.”
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:3: Meera's smile softened a little. He placed his hand on her hand. “And I thought you would never understand how much I love you.” Both kept looking at each other for some time and then laughed together.
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:4: Meera lay down with her head resting on the soft pillow placed behind her, but she did not leave Aarav's hand. When Aarav bent close to her, Meera lovingly placed her hand on the back of his neck. “Still scared?” he asked mischievously.
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:5: “Yes,” said Aarav, “so that I never become the reason for your smile.” Meera nodded. “You idiot, you had become the reason for my smile long ago.” Hearing her words, there was such happiness in Aarav's eyes which did not need any answer.
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:6: The small lamp burning in the room was spreading soft light on their faces. Meera's earrings moved slightly and Aarav's eyes stopped on her face. She asked softly, “Tell me one thing truthfully, that day you held my hand intentionally, right?”
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:7: Meera laughed. “Yes, and you were so naive that you thought I was going to fall.” Aarav also smiled. “I wish I would have understood then.” “Then perhaps today's story would not have been such a lovely story,” Meera said looking at him.
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:8: Aarav held her hand more lovingly, as if he had found his whole world in that answer. Now there was only a few inches of distance left between them.
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:9: Meera lowered her eyes, but the smile on her lips was saying everything. Aarav came a little closer and whispered, “My dearest friend, always keep smiling like this.”
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:10: Meera replied softly, “As long as you are with me, this smile will not go anywhere.” Aarav gently touched his forehead to hers.
en:jab-dosti-mohabbat-bani:11: The world outside kept moving at its own pace, but it was as if time stood still for them in that room. Their relationship, which started from an old friendship, was now turning into a new love every day, and all they needed that evening was each other's company.

en:summary:bas-ek-ichchha: The light of the yellow lamp burning in the room was very relaxing that night.
en:bas-ek-ichchha:0: The light of the yellow lamp burning in the room was very relaxing that night. Neha was smiling in yellow saree with her head on the pillow. Her husband Aarav bent close and lovingly brought his forehead close to her cheek.
en:bas-ek-ichchha:1: Neha closed her eyes, as if the fatigue of the whole day was lost somewhere in that one moment. Aarav asked softly, "What's the matter, why are you so quiet today?" Neha laughed, “I am not silent, I just want this moment to last a little longer.”
en:bas-ek-ichchha:2: “Then we will not look at the clock today,” Aarav said smilingly. She held Neha's hand and the light tinkling of her bangles echoed in the room. Both remained close like this for some time, without any hurry.
en:bas-ek-ichchha:3: Then Neha got up and sat on the edge of the bed and started adjusting the pallu of her saree. Aarav sat in front of her and smiled and held the end of the saree. "Wait, let me help," he said.
en:bas-ek-ichchha:4: Neha looked at him, "Do you even know how to handle the saree?" "No, but I can learn with you." Neha giggled at his words and then felt a little shy.
en:bas-ek-ichchha:5: Aarav carefully straightened the folds of the cloth, as if he was taking care of a delicate memory. Neha's eyes kept falling on his face again and again. She liked that Aarav was paying so much attention even to small things.
en:bas-ek-ichchha:6: Suddenly Neha said in a low voice, "Listen, fulfill one of my wishes today." Aarav looked at her with surprise, "Such a serious face? Tell me, what do you want?" Neha remained silent for a few moments and extended the end of the saree towards him.
en:bas-ek-ichchha:7: "I don't want any gift today," she said, "I just want a promise." "What kind of promise?" Aarav asked. "No matter how busy the day is, sit with me like this for a while at night."
en:bas-ek-ichchha:8: "No mobile, no work worries... just the two of us." Aarav's smile stopped for a moment; He didn't expect such a simple answer. He took one end of the saree from Neha's hand and said softly, "I will never consider this wish of yours small."
en:bas-ek-ichchha:9: Neha's eyes lit up, "Really?" “Yes, and starting right now,” Aarav replied. Both of them stood near the bed and started adjusting the soft folds of the saree.
en:bas-ek-ichchha:10: Neha looked down and smiled, and Aarav kept looking at her. There was no big surprise that night, nor any expensive gift.
en:bas-ek-ichchha:11: There was just a promise hidden in the folds of the yellow saree – every day a little time, a little companionship and a lot of love. Neha held his hand; Aarav also held her silently.

en:summary:patni-ki-ek-baat: The soft evening light was filtering through the window curtains and spreading into the room.
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:0: The soft evening light was filtering through the window curtains and spreading into the room. Nandini, sitting on the sofa, had the smell of jasmine flowers in her hair, and had a tired smile on her face. Her husband Sameer, sitting behind, gently gathered her in his arms.
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:1: Then he bent near her cheek and gave a light kiss, Nandini smiled shyly. “Big love is coming today?” He teased by rolling his eyes. Sameer laughed, “He comes as soon as he sees you, what is my fault in this?”
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:2: Nandini elbowed him lightly, but did not move away from his arms. Till a moment ago she was watching something on the phone; Now the phone was left just like that in his hand. Sameer placed his hand on her waist and asked, "What's the matter? Are you thinking about something today?"
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:3: Nandini looked towards the curtains, where the last light of the evening had stopped. “Yes,” he said softly, “there is one thing… but don't laugh.” Sameer came a little closer. “Have I ever laughed at what you said?”
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:4: “Many times,” Nandini said smiling, and their laughter filled the room. Then his voice became soft. “There are so many conversations throughout the day, so many tasks…” “But sometimes I just want to sit quietly with you for a while.”
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:5: Sameer took her fingers in his hand. “So sit, I am right here.” Nandini turned her head slightly and looked into his eyes. “That's all I wanted to say… I don't want anything big from you, I just want a little of your time.”
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:6: Sameer did not say anything for a few moments. He kept the phone nearby and took Nandini closer to him more affectionately than before. “I thought I would have to do something special to make you happy,” he said softly.
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:7: “But you just want me with you.” Nandini placed her hand on his hand. “Because you are the most special person to me.” Sameer rested his head on her shoulder and whispered near her ear, “So the whole evening is yours.”
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:8: Nandini giggled. “The whole evening? Won't you even check your phone in between?” “Not at all,” Sameer said laughing, “just you and me today.”
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:9: He then bent towards her, and Nandini moved her hair to one side, smiling. His fingers stopped on Sameer's hand; There was no need to say anything now.
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:10: The darkness outside gradually deepened, but a sweet warmth remained between them in the room. Nandini closed her eyes and placed her head on his shoulder.
en:patni-ki-ek-baat:11: Sameer held her, as if he did not want to let that small moment go anywhere. Nothing extraordinary happened that night; Just one true word from the wife brought both of them closer to each other again.

en:title:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan: One room, two friends and the truth of love
en:summary:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan: The full moon was shining outside the window and the golden threads of the room were scattering light on the pink bedsheet.
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:0: The full moon was shining outside the window and the golden threads of the room were scattering light on the pink bedsheet. Naina was sleeping on her side on the pillow in a green floral dress, completely unaware. On the other corner of the bed, her friend Riya was silently looking at Kabir, as if she wanted to say something.
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:1: Kabir leaned closer to her, Riya held his hand and their lips met for a moment. That little kiss was not the beginning of a new love, but the last question of an old relationship. Riya asked softly, “Kabir, do you still have the same place for me in your heart?”
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:2: Kabir lowered his eyes. “You are very special to me, but I don't want to lie to you.” Riya read his silence and looked towards sleeping Naina. “You like Naina, right?” he asked with a slight smile.
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:3: Kabir nodded. "For a long time. But I was afraid of hurting you." Riya's eyes became moist, then she said, "The pain is not caused by the truth, but by what is hidden. Now tell him the truth as well." Riya went out of the room on the pretext of getting water, so that both of them could get space to talk.
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:4: Kabir sat away from Naina for some time, then Naina slowly opened her eyes. “I was awake,” she said, “and I heard you.” Kabir got scared. “Naina, if you feel bad then I will leave right now.”
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:5: Naina stopped him and asked, “Why did you never tell me about your feelings?” “Because there was a fear of losing your friendship,” Kabir replied truthfully. Naina smiled. “And I thought, you will never be able to understand what my eyes say.”
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:6: Kabir sat near him, but he did not hurry. “Whatever was between Riya and me, we have ended it here today,” he said clearly. Naina looked into his eyes. “Then don’t hide anything from me.”
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:7: “Never,” said Kabir, “and if you want, we will start slowly.” Naina held his hand. “It probably started a long time ago.” Both laughed lightly; His hesitation started melting in the flickering light of the room.
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:8: Naina allowed him to come closer to her and Kabir placed a very soft kiss on her lips. There were no big promises in that moment, just the relief of being true to each other. Naina smiled and said, “You know, I wanted to remember such a moonlit night for a long time.”
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:9: Kabir asked, “And now?” “Now this will probably become my fondest memory,” she replied softly.
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:10: After some time, Naina again lay down on her side and Kabir came and curled up behind her. He held Naina's hand, gave a light kiss near her hair and let her sleep peacefully.
en:ek-kamra-do-saheliyan:11: The moon was still shining outside the window, but an old hesitation had gone from the hearts of both of them. That night their story began not with any secret, but with truth, trust and a soft smile.
